messages:
sara: FinServCo seeing intermittent 429s around 2026-02-10 18:01 UTC. Customer pasted one request id: 01AZF7Y2. They report spikes for ~10m windows. Can we collect repro evidence?

kevin: Thanks @sara. Can you ask for a curl + full response headers and one timestamped example (UTC)? We need x-rw-request-id and any x-rate-limit headers.

sara: Pasted customer's response headers:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-request-id: 01AZF7Y2
x-rate-limit-limit: 600
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 1676062860
retry-after: 30
content-type: application/json
``` 
They also attached a rough timeline: 18:00:05, 18:00:15, 18:00:26 all 429s.

kevin: Ok. Ask them to run a curl that preserves headers so we can verify. Example to send:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: 01AZF7Y2" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" --compressed
```
Tell them to capture stdout/stderr and paste.

devon: From infra, if they have bursts hitting the shared-hosted pool, we should see prefix-based rate-limiter triggers in our proxy logs. Ask for the proxy id in the response headers (x-proxy-id) if present. Also request a HAR from their browser or a tcpdump if they can.

sara: Customer sent a HAR (attached) and one curl output. Curl shows same headers + body: { "error": "rate_limited" }. I'll upload to S3 link and share.

kevin: Good. @devon can you grep the proxy logs for x-rw-request-id 01AZF7Y2 between 1676062800 and 1676062920? That covers their reported window.

ops-bot: running search job job-7821 for request id 01AZF7Y2 across prod proxies.

devon: Found matching entries on proxy p-13 and p-17. Sample log:
```
[2026-02-10T18:00:15.312Z] proxy=p-13 lvl=warn resp=429 req_id=01AZF7Y2 route=/v1/generate client_ip=35.204.12.99 limit=600 remaining=0 window_reset=1676062860
```
Looks like client exceeded per-minute window; remaining dropped to 0 and requests within same window got 429s.

kevin: That aligns. Ask customer for exact request pattern (are they fan-out-ing parallel calls?) Also check that they aren't sending multiple tokens/clients from same IP which would aggregate.

sara: Customer says it's a background job that spikes when their batch job runs — they confirmed 30 parallel workers at 18:00.

maria: Suggest they implement jittered backoff and honor retry-after. For immediate repro evidence, we should include a timeline table (UTC) and the first/last 429 request ids so SRE can correlate across systems.

kevin: Next actions:
- @sara: get full HAR + curl (done)
- @devon: collect proxy logs + rate limiter counters (in progress)
- @maria: prepare suggested retry/backoff snippet for them
- Ask customer to run a short replay with concurrency=1 to show baseline success rate.

sara: I'll send the replay instruction and ask them to run single-threaded curl for 60s and upload logs.

kevin: Thanks. Once we have replay + logs we'll prepare a ticket for capacity/quotas team. If it's confirmed burst from their side, recommend reserved capacity for predictable throughput.

sara: Noted. I'll update ticket with S3 link to HAR and curl and the replay results when available. :thumbsup:
